label: Slop-heavy email draft
input:
Hi Priya,

I hope this email finds you well. In today's fast-paced world, staying on top of infrastructure costs has become more important than ever before.

I wanted to reach out in order to share some findings from the cloud spend review we ran last quarter. It is important to note that this work was a collaborative effort across several teams. We really wanted to make sure we left no stone unturned.

Our analysis found that 41% of our EC2 spend went to instances that sat below 5% CPU for the entire month. The three largest offenders were the staging cluster, the nightly ETL fleet, and a set of orphaned load balancers from the 2023 migration. Switching the staging cluster to t4g.medium and shutting the ETL fleet down outside its window would save roughly $18,400 a month.

Data plays a crucial role in decisions like these. Whether or not we act on it, the numbers are worth understanding. It's worth noting that these numbers are a snapshot, not a trend.

We will need approval from finance before we can proceed. I have attached the full breakdown, and I would be happy to walk through it whenever works for you.

In conclusion, there is a meaningful opportunity here to reduce spend without affecting production. Each and every one of these changes is reversible. Let me know your thoughts.

Thanks,
Anjan
